*PharmaCraft Daily - 24 Oct 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Chemotherapy)
Q: Red-orange discolouration of body fluids is caused by?
Ans: Rifampicin
Why: Rifampicin causes harmless red-orange colouring of urine, sweat and tears. It is a potent enzyme inducer.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Immunopharmacology)
Q: Cyclosporine acts by inhibiting?
Ans: Calcineurin
Why: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus inhibit calcineurin, reducing IL-2 and T-cell activation. Nephrotoxicity is a key concern.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Toxicology)
Q: Antidote for iron poisoning is?
Ans: Deferoxamine
Why: Deferoxamine chelates iron in acute iron overdose. Dimercaprol/penicillamine are used for other heavy metals.

🌍 *FMGE* (General Pharmacology)
Q: A drug that binds a receptor and produces no effect but blocks the agonist is a?
Ans: Antagonist
Why: An antagonist binds the receptor without activating it and prevents the agonist from acting.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Recent Advances)
Q: CAR-T cell therapy is primarily used in?
Ans: Certain haematological cancers
Why: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy re-engineers patient T cells against tumour antigens (e.g. CD19 in B-cell malignancies).
